L0@P0: INDUCING AND UNIQUE ERGODICITY OF DOUBLE ROTATIONS
L1@P0: H. BRUIN AND G. CLACK
L2@P0: Abstract. In this paper we investigate “double rotations”, i.e., interval translation maps that
L3@P0: when considered on the circle, have just two intervals of continuity. Using the induction procedure
L4@P0: described by Suzuki et al., we show that Lebesgue a.e. double rotation is of finite type, i.e., it
L5@P0: reduces to an interval exchange transformation. However, the set of infinite type double rotations
L6@P0: is shown to have Hausdorff dimension strictly between 2 and 3, and carries a natural inductioninvariant measure. It is also shown that non-unique ergodicity of infinite type double rotations,
L7@P0: although occurring, is a-typical with respect to every induction-invariant probability measure in
L8@P0: parameter space.

L11@P0: introduced by Boshernitzan and Kornfeld in 1995, [BK]. They are a class of piecewise isometry
L12@P0: constructed by partitioning an interval, I (usually [0, 1)) into d subintervals and applying a rotation
L13@P0: to each partition element. Unlike IETs these rotations are not such that the map is surjective.
